## Chronological account of the episode

### The task / starting point
On **2026-03-05 12:55 UTC**, an issue (**#36142**, "Silent empty response when LLM rate limit hits mid-turn (after tool calls)") was filed against `openclaw/openclaw` by account `JaewookYou`. The repo runs the OpenClaw harness on model `anthropic/claude-opus-4-6` (per the issue's Environment block).

The issue body was unusually complete for a bug report — it read like a finished engineering write-up rather than a user complaint:
- **Bug:** when the LLM API returns a 429/overload **after tool calls in a turn have already completed**, the assistant turn comes back completely empty — no text, no error surfaced to the user, conversation appears dead.
- **Repro:** run 5+ concurrent opus sub-agents to burn rate-limit quota; in the main session run a turn with tool calls; the follow-up LLM call (to turn tool results into text) hits the rate limit.
- **Root cause (already pinpointed):** in `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution.ts`, the post-run error guard only checks for context-overflow errors (the earlier #26905 fix). Rate-limit/overload errors arriving mid-turn fall through, and the runner returns `kind: "success"` with empty payloads. The pre-tool-call path handles rate limits; the mid-turn path does not.
- **Evidence:** gateway logs showing `embedded run agent end: isError=true error=⚠️ API rate limit reached.` and `FailoverError: ⚠️ API rate limit reached.`, with no corresponding user-facing message.
- **Proposed fix + sign-off:** "Extend the existing #26905 context-overflow guard to also catch rate limit, overload, and generic embedded errors when no payload text was generated. **PR incoming.**"

### Two fixes opened in parallel (within minutes of the issue)
Rather than one follow-up, **two separate PRs** were opened almost immediately, both claiming to close #36142:

**PR #36193** — `fix(agent): surface rate limit / overload embedded errors mid-turn`, author `RealKai42` (commits by "Kaiyi"), created **2026-03-05 13:28** (~33 min after the issue).
- Scope was far larger than the issue: **14 files, +337/−47, 8 commits**. Only one commit (`5b83633`) actually addressed the rate-limit guard. The other seven touched unrelated subsystems: provider/model registry override resolution (`pi-embedded-runner/model.ts`), config key-stripping (`config/validation.ts`, `legacy.rules.ts`), Matrix `M_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` retry (`matrix/send.ts`), SQLite WAL journaling (`memory/manager-sync-ops.ts`), Discord preflight audio abort (`discord/monitor/preflight-audio.ts`), Telegram media-group retry (`telegram/bot-handlers.ts`), gateway channel-health policy, and a `skill-creator/SKILL.md` description change.
- The core fix itself: widen the guard from context-overflow-only to `finalEmbeddedError && !hasPayloadText`, plus new branches calling `isRateLimitErrorMessage` / `isOverloadedErrorMessage` returning a `kind: "final"` user-facing message.
- **Review signals:** Greptile gave 4/5, calling the core fix sound but docking it because the live end-to-end test was unchecked and no unit tests covered the new branches. Codex flagged a **P2 bug in the bundled config change** — the new unknown-key stripping loop stops traversal on arrays, so paths like `agents.list.0` are never cleaned and still hard-fail at startup (a defect in code unrelated to the rate-limit bug).
- **Outcome:** closed **2026-03-06 18:50**, never merged.

**PR #36206** — `fix(auto-reply): surface rate-limit and overload errors mid-turn with post-turn flush`, author `openperf`, created **2026-03-05 13:37** (~9 min after #36193). Labeled `r: too-many-prs`, `size: S`.
- Tightly scoped: **1 file, +73/−7** (`agent-runner-execution.ts` only).
- Went through a full review cycle. Greptile and Codex raised three concrete issues on commit `50ac2a1`:
  1. (Greptile) Silent-failure hole: the generic fallback was guarded by `if (errMsg)`, so an embedded error with an empty/undefined message would still fall through to `return { kind: "success" }` — the exact bug the PR was meant to fix.
  2. (Greptile) `blockReplyPipeline.stop()` called before `pendingToolTasks` were awaited (ordering fragility).
  3. (Codex) Unbounded `Promise.allSettled(pendingToolTasks)` could block the error path indefinitely.
- The author addressed all three in follow-up commits (final `92565d8`): moved `stop()` after the drain with optional chaining, added an unconditional catch-all `kind: "final"` return, and wrapped the drain in a 5s `Promise.race` timeout. Greptile re-reviewed and approved: *"The implementation looks solid… Ship it! 🚢"*
- **Outcome:** despite approval, auto-closed **2026-03-06 19:01** by bot `openclaw-barnacle`: *"Closing this PR because the author has more than 10 active PRs in this repo. Please reduce the active PR queue…"* Never merged.

### Where it ended
- Neither PR was merged. Bot `openclaw-barnacle` later marked the issue **stale due to inactivity**, then **closed it** with a generic "retry on the latest release" message.
- Issue #36142 final state: **CLOSED, NOT_PLANNED**, closed **2026-04-22 04:33**, labeled `stale`.

### Net observable result
A bug that was correctly and precisely diagnosed (down to the file, the fall-through path, and the originating #26905 fix) produced **two near-simultaneous, overlapping fix PRs for the same one-file change**. One was a sprawling 14-file/8-commit bundle that mixed the fix with seven unrelated changes and introduced a separate config-validation defect; it was closed unmerged. The other was correctly scoped, survived a full review iteration, and was approved — then auto-closed purely because its author already had >10 open PRs. The promised, review-approved fix never landed, and the issue was ultimately closed as not-planned.

I have enough to write the account. Here is a chronological, fact-based reconstruction drawn from issue #36142 and the two pull requests it references.

---

## Chronological account of the episode

### The task / starting point
On **2026-03-05 12:55 UTC**, an issue (**#36142**, "Silent empty response when LLM rate limit hits mid-turn (after tool calls)") was filed against `openclaw/openclaw` by account `JaewookYou`. The repo runs the OpenClaw harness on model `anthropic/claude-opus-4-6` (per the issue's Environment block).

The issue body was unusually complete for a bug report — it read like a finished engineering write-up rather than a user complaint:
- **Bug:** when the LLM API returns a 429/overload **after tool calls in a turn have already completed**, the assistant turn comes back completely empty — no text, no error surfaced to the user, conversation appears dead.
- **Repro:** run 5+ concurrent opus sub-agents to burn rate-limit quota; in the main session run a turn with tool calls; the follow-up LLM call (to turn tool results into text) hits the rate limit.
- **Root cause (already pinpointed):** in `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution.ts`, the post-run error guard only checks for context-overflow errors (the earlier #26905 fix). Rate-limit/overload errors arriving mid-turn fall through, and the runner returns `kind: "success"` with empty payloads. The pre-tool-call path handles rate limits; the mid-turn path does not.
- **Evidence:** gateway logs showing `embedded run agent end: isError=true error=⚠️ API rate limit reached.` and `FailoverError: ⚠️ API rate limit reached.`, with no corresponding user-facing message.
- **Proposed fix + sign-off:** "Extend the existing #26905 context-overflow guard to also catch rate limit, overload, and generic embedded errors when no payload text was generated. **PR incoming.**"

### Two fixes opened in parallel (within minutes of the issue)
Rather than one follow-up, **two separate PRs** were opened almost immediately, both claiming to close #36142:

**PR #36193** — `fix(agent): surface rate limit / overload embedded errors mid-turn`, author `RealKai42` (commits by "Kaiyi"), created **2026-03-05 13:28** (~33 min after the issue).
- Scope was far larger than the issue: **14 files, +337/−47, 8 commits**. Only one commit (`5b83633`) actually addressed the rate-limit guard. The other seven touched unrelated subsystems: provider/model registry override resolution (`pi-embedded-runner/model.ts`), config key-stripping (`config/validation.ts`, `legacy.rules.ts`), Matrix `M_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` retry (`matrix/send.ts`), SQLite WAL journaling (`memory/manager-sync-ops.ts`), Discord preflight audio abort (`discord/monitor/preflight-audio.ts`), Telegram media-group retry (`telegram/bot-handlers.ts`), gateway channel-health policy, and a `skill-creator/SKILL.md` description change.
- The core fix itself: widen the guard from context-overflow-only to `finalEmbeddedError && !hasPayloadText`, plus new branches calling `isRateLimitErrorMessage` / `isOverloadedErrorMessage` returning a `kind: "final"` user-facing message.
- **Review signals:** Greptile gave 4/5, calling the core fix sound but docking it because the live end-to-end test was unchecked and no unit tests covered the new branches. Codex flagged a **P2 bug in the bundled config change** — the new unknown-key stripping loop stops traversal on arrays, so paths like `agents.list.0` are never cleaned and still hard-fail at startup (a defect in code unrelated to the rate-limit bug).
- **Outcome:** closed **2026-03-06 18:50**, never merged.

**PR #36206** — `fix(auto-reply): surface rate-limit and overload errors mid-turn with post-turn flush`, author `openperf`, created **2026-03-05 13:37** (~9 min after #36193). Labeled `r: too-many-prs`, `size: S`.
- Tightly scoped: **1 file, +73/−7** (`agent-runner-execution.ts` only).
- Went through a full review cycle. Greptile and Codex raised three concrete issues on commit `50ac2a1`:
